content:
I'd like to introduce hopscotch, a CLI tool that you can run in any Lean project, which given a range of versions of a dependency (namely: a range of lake inputRevs), validates a project against them (namely: runs lake update <dependency> + lake build), bisecting to find the exact commit that breaks the your project .

The tool is a standalone CLI tool; you can clone the repo and build it from source, or grab a binary from the latest release (caveat: this has been battle-tested on Ubuntu only)

The original motivation, beside downstream break detection, is to provide a mechanism to easily update dependents of mathlib4 (but it works on any direct dependency required on the lakefile.), which has a lot of churn, by pinpointing and fixing breaking changes one by one, with the added context of exactly which change introduced a break.

For example, one might run in it like hopscotch dep mathlib --to v4.29.0 to 'try to make it' to v4.29.0 and see where conflict arises.

It's designed for interactive use: it stops when encountering a "failure boundary", reports it, and leaves your workspace in the state where you can work on a fix, commit, and repeat until satisfied.

The README has a step-by-step example that walks through this workflow.

The tool is very much in its infancy so any feedback is appreciated. The intention is to accommodate different workflows that maintainers might be used to, making it easier to keep dependencies up to date.
